newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Sberbank says votes 5.0 pct foreign cap.
newsitem.headline: Russia Sberbank says votes 5.0 pct foreign cap.

text.p: Russia's largest bank Sberbank has voted to limit foreign-registered shareholdings to five percent of capital, though the central bank has not registered the change, a senior bank official said on Thursday.

"Shareholders at the May 30 meeting made changes to the charter, setting the total (non-resident) quota at five percent of issued shares," Securities Department Head Vladimir Pavlov told Reuters. "Within the five percent not more than one percent may be held by each non-resident."
The shareholders' meeting was a closed one and Pavlov was making the information public for the first time.
Pavlov said the new charter was not yet registered by the central bank to become law. He said that currently, no foreign-registered companies were listed as Sberbank shareholders.
Sberbank, with a market capitalisation of about $3.0 billion, is the only liquid bank share in a very illiquid Russian bank share market.

It is one of the most actively traded shares on the market and its price doubled a few weeks ago. Analysts forecast a further rise. On the Russian Trading System Sberbank slipped to $296.00 from $302.00 at Wednesday's close.
